Exercise: V-Bar Pulldown

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
pull

Difficulty Level:
intermediate

Movement Patterns:

- horizontal_pulling

Primary Muscles:

- lats

Secondary Muscles:

- biceps
- middle back
- shoulders

Equipment:

- cable

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
moderate to high

Recovery Time:
48 hours

Goals:

- improving_shoulder_stability
- enhancing_bicep_engagement
- developing_lats_and_middle_back_strength

Contraindications:
None

Exercise Variations:

- name: Wide Grip V-Bar Pulldown, force: pull, level: intermediate, mechanic: compound, primaryMuscles: ['lats'], secondaryMuscles: ['biceps', 'middle back', 'shoulders']
- name: Narrow Grip V-Bar Pulldown, force: pull, level: intermediate, mechanic: compound, primaryMuscles: ['lats'], secondaryMuscles: ['biceps', 'middle back', 'shoulders']

Substitution Options:

- name: Lat Pulldown, equipment: cable
- name: Pull-Up, equipment: bar

Instructions:

- Sit down on a pull-down machine with a V-Bar attached to the top pulley.
- Adjust the knee pad of the machine to fit your height. These pads will prevent your body from being raised by the resistance attached to the bar.
- Grab the V-bar with the palms facing each other (a neutral grip). Stick your chest out and lean yourself back slightly (around 30-degrees) in order to better engage the lats. This will be your starting position.
- Using your lats, pull the bar down as you squeeze your shoulder blades. Continue until your chest nearly touches the V-bar. Exhale as you execute this motion. Tip: Keep the torso stationary throughout the movement.
- After a second hold on the contracted position, slowly bring the bar back to the starting position as you breathe in.
- Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions.
